result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the real issue: the reset button looks like Save and sits next to it. Both suggest moving it, restyling it and adding a confirmation, and both pile on far more points than a four-section page needs. A wins because it has fewer manufactured issues and ends by calling everything else polish. B uses an audit format with severity labels and an assumptions block, and it labels a 'Major' issue about missing accessible names and grouping that its own text admits the markup doesn't support. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly flag the identical, side-by-side reset button as the main issue and suggest separating it, restyling it and adding a confirmation, but both turn into long audits out of proportion to a small page. A labels its findings Blocker and Major, and one of them, 'no accessible names', is wrong because the markup has labels, as A itself admits later. B lists even more secondary points, but it frames them correctly ('the rest is polish') and makes no false claims about the markup, so it wins narrowly.
